clue.text: Finding key among change could result in cross words

indicators.note: among puts the key letter in the middle of the word for change

parts.note: a change is an alteration
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Finding the right key amid all this change might lead to cross words in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross words' looks like crossword answers, but it means angry words: a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated quarrel is an exchange of angry words.

clue.text: Figure on a new temporary provision

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a figure

indicators.note: new says the letters of 'on a' are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A figure is placed on a new provision that will only last a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ON A into OAN, which follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lent is provided only for a time before being given back.

clue.text: He puts out that a point's been awarded to the winner

parts.note: E (east) is a point of the compass
a victor is the winner of a contest

explanation.surface: A point has been awarded to the winning player in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He puts out' means one who throws tenants out of a property, not a cricketer or fireman.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who removes tenants from a home is said to evict them.

clue.text: Fish with a musical tail!

parts.note: the cod is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: A fish that comes with a tune at its tail end.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing passage of a piece of music is its tailpiece, named from the Italian word for tail.

clue.text: Had in mind a trifle

explanation.surface: Someone had a mere trifle in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something in mind is to have considered it; 'a thought' also means a little bit, as in 'a thought too salty'.

clue.text: A man who's not settled, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a bill not settled is still owing, said casually as 'owin''

explanation.surface: A man who has not paid his debts, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Said with a dropped final G, OWING sounds like the Welsh man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen is a male first name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: Spy coming clean, revealing unofficial financial dealings

parts.note: James Bond is fiction's best-known spy
washing is getting clean

explanation.surface: A spy confesses all and exposes some shady money deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming clean' suggests confessing; here it simply means being washed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond washing is the practice of selling securities before a dividend and buying back after, to dodge tax.

clue.text: They'll go back all the same

definitions.text: They'll go back all the same

parts.words: They'll go back all the same
parts.note: words or phrases that read identically when taken from the end to the start

explanation.surface: People who will return regardless of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like 'level' read the same in either direction, so going back gives the same result.

clue.text: Domestic pets can rip seats to pieces!

indicators.note: tearing something to pieces breaks up the letters of these words into a new order

explanation.surface: House pets are able to tear the chair seats apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-haired house cats of a breed from Iran are kept as pets.

clue.text: Statice will make an impression on a salesman

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: a seal is an impression stamped into wax
a vender (vendor) is one who sells

explanation.surface: Something will leave a mark on a travelling salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statice' is a plant name, not a word about stillness.
explanation.definitionFit: Statice is another name for the coastal plant genus Limonium, with papery flowers.

clue.text: Here's a jolly team's to get salute

parts.note: present means here, as in answering a register
a jolly is a Royal Marine, so a team of them is RMs

explanation.surface: Here is a cheerful team getting a salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine (RM), not an adjective for cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding rifles upright before the body is a formal military salute.

clue.text: One compound will accommodate ten animals

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the mixed letters hold the next piece
compound means mixed together, so the letters of 'one' are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: One farm compound has room for ten beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' rearranges ONE into OEN, and 'will accommodate' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle used for draught work, an example of animals.

clue.text: Point to a listener, that's close by

parts.note: N (north) is a point of the compass
the ear is the organ one listens with

explanation.surface: Point at someone listening who is standing close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by is nearby or at hand.

clue.text: Form void — was made to repudiate

indicators.note: form as an instruction says to shape these letters into something new

explanation.surface: A form declared void was drawn up just so it could be rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate something is to deny any link with it.

clue.text: West Indies scout stranded

parts.note: a scout sent ahead is a spy

explanation.surface: A scout from the West Indies is left stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranded' means made of thin strands, not marooned.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that is thin and in strands is described as straggly and fine.

clue.text: Such a blissful meal must include wine

indicators.note: must include says the letters are found running through the words just before

explanation.surface: Such a perfect dinner needs some wine to go with it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dry white Burgundy wine from northern France.

clue.text: Ground rent?

parts.note: read as a tear or split in the earth, not money paid for land

explanation.surface: A query about the charge paid for leasehold land.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep fissure in the earth is a rent in the ground.

clue.text: Blue would be appropriate

explanation.surface: Being blue would be suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is the colour of the Conservatives, the political right wing; right also means fitting or correct.

clue.text: The first man to be a mother?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Was the first man ever to become a mother?
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, he was the first human created.

clue.text: Getting a number over the river

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
on means over, on top of

explanation.surface: Taking a number of people across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Avon is a river, most famously the one at Stratford in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is a name borne by several English rivers.

clue.text: On reflection writing a few last words when fit

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: MS is manuscript, a piece of writing
PS (postscript) is the last words of a letter

explanation.surface: After some thought, writing a few final words when feeling well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reverses MS + A + PS (MSAPS) to give the answer; 'fit' is a seizure, not healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden convulsion or seizure is a fit.

clue.text: Heartless woman, a cheat, responsible for a flyer

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for woman is taken out

parts.note: she refers to a woman
to gull is to dupe or cheat

explanation.surface: A heartless woman, a fraud, is to blame for a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' drops H from SHE, leaving SE; 'a flyer' is a bird, not a leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: This seabird is a familiar creature of the air at the coast.

clue.text: The painter's dull — without craft, that is

parts.note: mat (matt) means dull, not shiny

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside puts the letters for 'that is' around the craft

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is
SS is a steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: The painter is boring, lacking any skill, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: IE goes round SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: An artist bearing in game

indicators.note: in places the bearing letter inside the word for the game

parts.note: hockey is a team game
N (north) is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A painter carries himself well during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: David Hockney is an English artist.
explanation.definitionFit: David Hockney is a celebrated English painter.

clue.text: A battle involving colour

explanation.surface: A fight involving flags or colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta in Italy was the scene of an 1859 battle, after which the purplish-red dye was named.

clue.text: Ginger biscuits or crackers?

explanation.surface: Are ginger biscuits a kind of cracker?
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger nuts are a British biscuit, so 'Ginger biscuits' gives the second word of that name; 'crackers' means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger nuts are hard spiced biscuits; crackers and nuts are both slang for crazy.

clue.text: A northerner's way to go about business

indicators.note: go about means surround, so the letters for way are placed round the business

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: How a man from the north goes about his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Scotland lives in Britain's far north.

clue.text: Here's the pirate captain's sidekick — duck!

explanation.surface: Here is the pirate captain's sidekick, telling you to get your head down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck!' looks like an order to stoop but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: In Peter Pan, Smee is Captain Hook's bosun; smee is also a dialect name for some wild ducks such as the wigeon.

clue.text: Given appropriate backing, are prolific

indicators.note: backing says the word for appropriate is set down backwards

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or appropriate

explanation.surface: With proper support, they produce a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abundant or swarming is to exist in great numbers.

clue.text: Try running water

explanation.surface: Give some flowing water a go.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something is to put it to a trial; the Test is a river, a body of flowing water.

clue.text: An organiser of the young put at customers' disposal

indicators.note: putting letters at someone's disposal lets them be arranged freely

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's goods put at shoppers' disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposal' rearranges AT and CUSTOMERS; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: He leads a troop of Scouts, a youth movement.

clue.text: Attending every sporting contest whatever the situation

explanation.surface: A fan who goes to every sporting fixture regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, it means being present at every fixture; as an idiom it means in any case.
